name: dev/shared-machine
preview: When you are about to run a test suite or start a vite dev server in heart-rush-tools, read this because play's tests can exhaust the Mac's ephemeral ports and break every app on the machine, and stale dev servers from finished agents pile up.

revisions.author: 3zl47w7d-mvhfwmuj-a16b6656
revisions.body:
# Tests and dev servers on Silas's Mac

Several agents and Silas share one machine. A test run or dev server that leaks processes or sockets breaks his browser and other apps, not just your work.

## Play's test suite

`apps/play`'s `test` script runs `tsx --test --test-concurrency=1 test/*.test.ts` on purpose. Each test file opens its own workerd through wrangler's `getPlatformProxy()` (`apps/play/test/db.ts`), and miniflare's proxy to workerd uses an undici connection pool with no cap. Under CPU contention that pool runs away: one workerd reached 25,000 ESTABLISHED loopback sockets, and 16 workerds in parallel used up the Mac's whole ephemeral port range (49152–65535). Every other program that opens a connection then fails — the browser, 1Password, GitHub.

- Never raise `--test-concurrency` or drop it, and never run test files in parallel by hand.
- Never run two suites at the same time (play twice, or play beside another app's suite), and never start one while another heavy run — a full `pnpm build`, a Playwright run, another agent's suite — is going. Check with `pgrep -fl workerd` and `pgrep -fl "tsx --test"` first.
- A failure containing `EADDRNOTAVAIL` means the port range is used up. Stop every workerd you started, wait for the sockets to drain (`netstat -an -p tcp | grep -c ESTABLISHED` falls back to the low hundreds), then run once, alone.
- Observed with wrangler 4.151.2, workerd 1.20261019.1 and miniflare 5.20261019.0-beta. A newer version is not a reason to raise the concurrency without measuring sockets during a full run.

Other suites: `packages/rules-engine` and `packages/northlight` have `test` scripts (plain `tsx --test`, no workerd). `apps/tools` and `apps/rules` have no test directory. Play's `test` script first builds `@heartrush/content` and runs `wrangler types`; see [[heart-rush-tools/play/content-catalogue]] for why that order matters.

## Dev servers

- Before starting one, run `pgrep -fl "vite dev"` and `crtr dev service status`. Reuse a server that is already serving your checkout instead of starting a second one.
- One dev server per agent. Port 3912 (play's source port) is Silas's own; never start on it, never kill what is on it. Pick a free port.
- Before you finish — `push final` or yielding — kill every `vite dev` you started, the workerd it spawned, and any browser you launched with `crtr capture tab launch` (`crtr capture tab quit`). A finished node's server keeps running and holding ports and memory until someone notices.
